You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 2-week-old infant is brought to the pediatrician for the first time by his parents. His mother received regular prenatal care and the child was born at home under the guidance of a midwife and a doula. The child appears well. The parents tell you they do not plan to have their child receive any vaccines. After a discussion regarding the risks and benefits of vaccines, the parents are still adamant in their wishes to forgo. Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

Options:
A. Call child protective services
B. Refuse to continue to care for the child
C. Seek a court order to deliver the vaccines against the wishes of the parents
D. Give any scheduled vaccines during that visit against the will of the parents
E. Document the visit, specifically the detailing of risks and benefits and the parents' refusal of treatment
